title: BuildMap job package
description: The hand-off contract between Paul's agent and the BuildMap website. One buildmap.json per job, at the root of the job folder. Level 1 (the one-page Lite report) and Level 2 (the detailed report) come from one assessment run and are generated together; what the customer has paid for is recorded separately under access and never changes the findings. Level 3 is separately commissioned. A job can carry several mutually exclusive options (subdivision or townhouses); they are never added together. Passing this schema means the package is well formed. It does not mean the planning findings are right or that anything is approved.

job.description: Created by the BuildMap order form. Paul's agent never changes these fields. Corrections to the site go in site.corrections with their evidence.

id.description: BM-<yyyymmdd>-<slug>, also the job folder name

slug.description: Becomes the website folder and pitch-<slug>.vercel.app

brief.description: The client's own words: what they want, worries, must-haves

package.description: True when the client ordered the full package: website, marketing assets, strategy and feasibility

account_requested.description: The client asked for a BuildMap account: first basic report free, then half price

development_type.description: What the customer asked us to look at. townhouses and infill mean the same thing (homes built on the site); new orders use townhouses.

brief_version.description: Version of the default brief the customer accepted

site.description: Level 0: the automatic site record pulled from the address. Paul's agent may correct it and must say so in sources.

land_area_m2.description: Headline area. Say which one it is in land_area_basis.

areas.description: The different site areas, kept apart. Leave out any that is not known.

identity.description: How sure we are this is the right parcel.

corrections.description: Evidenced corrections to what the customer entered. The original stays in job.

website.description: Optional overrides from Ant or the client. Anything missing becomes a marked placeholder on the site.

lead_email.description: Where enquiries from the project website are sent: the client's existing email address

brand.description: The client's own branding, pulled from their website (Firecrawl branding format) so the project website is on-brand. Checked by a person before the site goes live.

logo.description: URL or file path of the logo

confirmed_by_client.description: The client has agreed to their logo and branding being used on the project website

options.description: Mutually exclusive ways to develop the site. Counts, areas and yields are never added across options.

selection.description: The one option chosen for the website and marketing. Only Paul (or the client through Paul) records this.

open_items.description: Everything still to check, for the whole job. A blocking item stops publication.

effect.description: What it could change: yield, layout, cost, pathway

owner_discipline.description: Who closes it: planner, surveyor, traffic engineer, lawyer...

images.description: Images that belong to the job or to options rather than to one level (site plans, option plans).

provenance.description: Where the figures came from: source report, hashes, page references. Free form.

sources.description: Every source used, each with an id that source_refs point at.

run.description: The one assessment run behind Level 1 and Level 2. Two runs are only comparable when these match.

source_snapshot.description: Id or date of the frozen source data

model.description: Model or deployment identifier, where available

access.description: Payment and permission, kept apart from the findings. Written by the website and by Paul, never by the assessment. A purchase never changes a finding and never gives permission to publish.

publication.description: A public marketing website is a separate decision from issuing a report.

status.description: How far this report has got. generated: produced by the agent. checked: passed the agent's own QA. reviewed: Paul has reviewed it. issued: Paul has signed it off (signed_off_by and signed_off_on are required). None of these says the customer has paid, and none says a council has approved anything.

file.description: Path relative to the job folder, e.g. level-1/images/ext-west.jpg

reuse_permitted.description: For third-party diagrams: true only when we have permission to republish

file.description: Separate image file, at least 2000 px on the long side. Never only inside the PDF.

artists_impression.description: true only for renders. A technical plan is not an artist's impression.

public.description: Older flag, still read: false means not public. Prefer visibility.

scale.description: e.g. '1:200 at A3'. Leave out if not to scale.

vector_file.description: The vector original, where one exists

disclaimer.description: Printed on the website wherever this level's content appears

signed_off_by.description: The person who approved this level for issue. A level is only treated as issued when this and signed_off_on are filled in.

issue_scope.description: What exactly was issued, e.g. 'Conditional desktop concept, holds as listed'. Never 'build-ready' or 'approved' unless that is what was signed.

report_pages.description: Page count of report_pdf. The Lite report is one page.

run_id.description: The assessment run this report came from. Level 1 and Level 2 share one run.

level1.description: Level 1: the Lite report. One page, made from the same assessment run as Level 2. It shows each option, the residential count, key areas and parking, a short zoning explanation and every material hold. No renders.

summary.description: 3-5 plain sentences: the headline answer for this site

option.description: e.g. Up to 3 homes of 3 storeys as a permitted activity

hazard.description: Flood, liquefaction, coastal, slope, contamination (HAIL), heritage, protected trees, easements...

level2.description: Level 2: the detailed report, generated together with Level 1 from the same run. Buying it gives access to it; it does not produce different findings or remove a qualification.

result.description: Use minor-breach only when a planner has said so; do not infer it.

option_ids.description: Which options this rule check applies to; leave out if it applies to the whole site

evidence_status.description: How good the evidence is, within the scope of the source

consent.description: What it means for consent. A model pass does not mean the development is permitted.

services.description: Water, wastewater, stormwater, power, fibre, access

level3.description: Level 3: the development plan. Separately commissioned, never produced from an address alone. Present only when it has actually been commissioned and produced.

summary.description: 2-4 plain sentences: what is proposed and why it suits the site

id.description: Stable id used by images and prices, e.g. apt-06

type_group.description: Residences with the same plan share this, e.g. 'Upper full-floor'

indicative_price_nzd.description: Only if Paul or the client supplies it; otherwise leave out

open_items.description: What is not yet checked: survey, consent, engineering. Never shown as a selling point.

evidence.description: How well the result is backed. source-report = taken from the report as written; authoring-calculation = the agent's own geometry maths; the last three need a named person or document in the note.

home.description: A home in an infill option.

footprint_m2.description: Roof or building envelope on the ground

floor_area_status.description: allowance = an envelope figure before any floor plan exists; never shown as the home's floor area

floor_area_allowance_m2.description: Envelope allowance only. Use with floor_area_status 'allowance'.

floor_area_m2.description: Only once a floor plan exists (status designed or measured)

floor_area_note.description: What the figure includes: garage, stairs, voids

lot.description: A vacant lot in a subdivision option. Lots have no bedrooms, bathrooms or floor area.

area_m2.description: Leave out if not known and say why in note. Never 0.

area_basis.description: mapped = measured off map geometry, not survey

kind.description: Only residential lots count as sections. A road lot is land, not yield.

building_test_note.description: What the building test was, e.g. '8 x 15 m rectangle fits'. This is a geometry test, not a designed house.

result.description: The model result only: whether the drawing fits the test. It says nothing about approval.

basis.description: geometric = the shape fits on the drawing; it is not a statement that the planning rule is met

evidence_status.description: How good the evidence is, within the scope of the source

consent.description: What it means for consent. A model pass does not mean the development is permitted.

standing.description: concept = drawn and fits, approvals outstanding; conditional = works only if named conditions are met; potential = known to fail a test as drawn and needs a consent departure

totals.description: For this option only. Leave a figure out if it is unknown; never write 0 for unknown.

lots.description: Residential lots only. Road and other lots are counted separately.

yield_label.description: highest-tested: the best layout found in a finite search. Only use verified-maximum when the evidence and analysis support it.

yield_note.description: The search, brief and evidence limits behind the yield

roof_coverage_basis.description: What was measured and what it was divided by

assumptions.description: Design assumptions as plain numbers, e.g. road_corridor_width_m

quantities.description: Any measured figure that needs its unit and basis kept with it.

basis.description: How it was measured and, for a percentage, what it was divided by

visibility.description: Who may see this. public: anyone. client: the customer entitled to this job and revision. internal: Paul and Ant only. The website enforces this on the server. If left out, treat as client.
